name: POST /api/leadflow/failures/dlq/replay - bounded and idempotent
description:
Replays dead-lettered items in a BOUNDED batch (4cc3f597-f6c8-4dc5-8044-096ce144e676#AC2). The cap is the point, not a pagination convenience: a queue that has been filling for six hours holds thousands of items, and replaying them all at once trips the provider's rate limit, refills the queue and - for a messaging connector - puts thousands of messages into inboxes in one minute. The count NOT replayed is returned, because a silent cap reads as "the queue is clear".

EACH REPLAY IS KEYED ON THE ITEM, so replaying a replay is one replay. A DLQ item delivered twice is exactly the duplicate the queue exists to avoid.

THE KILL SWITCH OUTRANKS THE REPLAY (4cc3f597-f6c8-4dc5-8044-096ce144e676#AC4). MEASURED LIVE: with the global send pause engaged the replay returned 409, because replaying a queue during a duplicate-send incident is the loop the switch was thrown to stop.

Failures are returned per item with their reason rather than as one aggregate count - "2 failed" cannot tell an operator whether to retry or to escalate, and "the circuit is open" and "the service returned 500" have different next steps.

QA NOTE: this runs in the same suite as the kill-switch test, which engages the global pause. The interlock is the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION — replaying a queue during a duplicate-send incident is the loop the switch was thrown to stop — so the suite asserts the 409 rather than racing the switch back off, which would test the opposite of the rule.

testCases.name: Replay is refused while the global send pause is engaged
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: ids must be a non-empty array of delivery ids
The global send pause is engaged, so nothing may be replayed. Release the kill switch first - replaying a queue during a duplicate-send incident is the loop the switch was thrown to stop.
Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
